🎨 Best Tools for Painting Contractors (2026)

A painting contractor wins work on estimates, and the estimate calls usually come in while you are on a ladder. For a small painting company, start with Jobber for estimates, scheduling and invoicing, Rosie, Upfirst or Dialzara to answer the phone when nobody can, and QuickBooks Online or Wave for the books. Jobber has its own painting contractor software page. None of the answering tools in our directory is built only for painters, so pick on price and call volume. Prices come from each vendor's own pricing page.

FAQ

What software does a small painting company need?Three things: a way to send estimates and schedule jobs, a way to catch estimate calls while you are on a job, and a way to invoice and keep the books. Jobber covers estimates, scheduling and invoicing; Rosie, Upfirst or Dialzara covers the phone; QuickBooks Online or Wave handles bookkeeping.
How much does painting contractor software cost?From our directory (vendor prices checked Oct 2026): Jobber Core $29/mo billed annually ($49 monthly), Rosie from $49/mo for 250 minutes, Upfirst from $24.95/mo for 30 calls, Dialzara from $29/mo for 60 minutes, QuickBooks Online Simple Start $38/mo list price, and Wave Starter $0.
Do I need an AI receptionist as a painting contractor?If estimate calls go to voicemail while you are painting, probably yes. Rosie gives 250 minutes for $49/mo, Upfirst Starter covers 30 calls for $24.95/mo, and Dialzara starts at $29/mo for 60 minutes with no contract. All three are general home-service answering tools, not painter-specific ones, so test one with a real estimate call before you commit.
Is there free software for painters?Wave Starter is free for invoicing and bookkeeping, and QuickBooks Online has a free plan limited to 1 user and 2 invoices a month. Estimating and scheduling apps like Jobber are paid but offer free trials.
